name: Dried Turmeric Fingers
short_description: Nizamabad and Erode fingers, curcumin 2–3% or 3–5% to order. Sortex cleaned, moisture max 10%, 25 kg and 50 kg bags, 18 MT in a 20ft.
long_description: Turmeric is bought on curcumin, not on looks. We hold two specifications — 2–3% for colour and culinary use, and 3–5% for extraction and nutraceutical buyers — and you nominate which one at order, because paying extraction money for culinary material is the most common way a first-time buyer loses margin on this product.

Nizamabad in Telangana gives high-curcumin material, Erode and Salem in Tamil Nadu give bright colour and consistent finger length, and Sangli in Maharashtra covers the bulk culinary grade. Fingers are boiled, sun-dried to below 10% moisture, polished, and Sortex cleaned to strip stones, soil and off-colour pieces before bagging.

The same crop is available as powder and as polished bulbs. Powder ships in the same 25 kg bags with an inner liner, and we run it on a dedicated line with a metal detector in place, because cross-contamination in ground spice is the complaint that ends a supplier relationship.

payment_terms: LC at sight, or 30% TT advance with balance against B/L copy
packing_note: Jute bags suit buyers who resell in bulk; PP woven with a liner holds moisture better on long or humid routes. Buyer-branded bags are available from 10 MT.

name: Dehydrated White Onion Flakes
short_description: Mahuva kibbled white onion, 8–15 mm flakes, moisture max 6%. SO2-free option. Low density — 8–9 MT in a 20ft, so plan the container before the price.
long_description: Mahuva in Gujarat is the centre of the world's dehydrated white onion trade, and the reason is the raw material: a local white onion with high solids and low pungency that dries to a pale ivory flake instead of browning. Buyers in Germany, the Netherlands and the USA use it in soup, seasoning and snack applications where colour matters as much as flavour.

Density is the thing importers get wrong on their first order. Onion flakes are light — a 20ft container fills on volume long before it reaches its weight limit, so it carries 8–9 MT, not the 18–20 MT a buyer might assume from a spice quotation. We size the container against the order rather than the other way round, and we say this at quotation stage.

Standard product is sulphited for colour retention. An SO2-free grade is available for buyers with a clean-label specification, at a slightly deeper ivory colour. Minced, granules, powder and toasted flakes run off the same line to the same specification.

name: Dehydrated Garlic Flakes & Granules
short_description: Root and skin free garlic from Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. Flakes, chopped, granules or powder, moisture max 6%, 20 kg cartons, 9 MT in a 20ft.
long_description: Dehydrated garlic sells on two things: how clean it is and how white it stays. Root plate and skin left in the product are what drag a lot down from food-grade to feed-grade, so material is peeled, inspected and air-classified before drying rather than after.

Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh supply the bulk of India's dehydration-grade garlic. We run four cuts off the same raw material — flakes, chopped, granules and powder — which means a buyer taking more than one particle size gets it from a single lot with a single certificate of analysis, instead of matching two suppliers' colour.

Powder and fine granules are the grades most likely to be blended, so both go through a metal detector and are held on a retained sample for the full shelf life. If a buyer's own QA disputes a result, we can pull the retained sample rather than argue about it.

name: Dried Red Chilli (Teja & Byadgi)
short_description: Guntur Teja at 75,000–100,000 SHU for heat, Byadgi at ASTA 70–120 for colour. Stem or stemless, moisture max 10%, 20 kg and 25 kg bales.
long_description: These are two different products that happen to be the same fruit. Teja S17 from the Guntur belt is bought for pungency — 75,000 to 100,000 Scoville — and goes into chilli powder, sauces and the Southeast Asian trade. Byadgi from Karnataka is bought for colour — ASTA 70 to 120 — with very little heat, and goes into oleoresin extraction and into dishes that need red without burn.

Buyers who order the wrong one usually asked for red chilli by weight and price. We quote both against the number that matters to the application, and will say plainly when a cheaper lot is the wrong tool for what the buyer described.

Both are available stem-on or stemless. Stemless costs more per kilo because the labour is real, but it ships more product per container and removes a cleaning step at the buyer's end, so on landed cost it is often the cheaper option. Material is dried to below 10% moisture and baled under pressure to keep the container efficient.

name: Dried Ginger (Whole & Sliced)
short_description: Cochin and Karnataka rhizomes, volatile oil 1.5–2.5%, moisture max 10%. Bold and non-bold grades, whole or sliced, 25 kg PP bags.
long_description: Cochin ginger has a trade name older than most of the companies buying it. What distinguishes it is volatile oil — 1.5 to 2.5% — which is where the aroma sits, and which is the specification an extraction buyer will hold you to even when a culinary buyer never asks.

Grades split on size. Bold rhizomes command a premium and go to buyers reselling whole spice; non-bold and split material goes to grinding and extraction where appearance is irrelevant. Sliced ginger dries faster and more evenly, which is why it is usually the better choice for a buyer who intends to grind it anyway.

Kerala and Karnataka material is sun-dried to below 10% moisture, cleaned, and graded before bagging. Sulphur bleaching is available for markets that expect a pale rhizome, but we default to unbleached and will tell a buyer which one their destination market actually wants.

name: Dried Moringa Leaf Powder
short_description: Shade-dried moringa leaf, 80–100 mesh, moisture max 8%. Vivid green, organic grade available, 20 kg double-lined cartons. MOQ 1 MT.
long_description: Colour is the specification buyers judge moringa on before they read the certificate of analysis, and colour is decided by drying method. Sun drying is cheaper and produces a dull olive powder with degraded nutrient content. We shade dry at controlled temperature, which costs more and holds the vivid green that a supplements buyer expects to see when they open the sample.

Leaf comes from Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, is destalked before drying, and is milled to 80–100 mesh. Stalk left in the leaf is the main reason a lot runs fibrous and grey, so destalking is done by hand and checked on a sample from each batch.

Organic certified material under NPOP and NOP is available on planned volumes with a longer lead time, because it comes from a separate grower group and a segregated line. Conventional material ships from stock at 1 MT minimum, which makes this the easiest product on our list to trial before committing.
packing: 20 kg export carton with double food-grade liner
shelf_life: 24 months in cool, dry storage away from light
payment_terms: LC at sight, or 30% TT advance with balance against B/L copy
packing_note: Double liner and opaque cartons protect colour, which degrades under light faster than it does under heat. Retail-ready pouch packing is available on request.
